title: Unveiling topology in imaging problems via quasi-isometry and persistent homology
summary: We show that the topological structures, such as loops, voids, and higher-dimensional holes of unknown objects (of flow of an object in space-time) can be recovered from noisy and indirect measurements. More precisely, we describe how the part of the persistent homology of a space can be determined from a noise-prone and discretized model space when there is a quasi-isometry between the original space and the space modeling indirect measurements.
